## Foxora AI v4.0.1 — engine-bundled, cross-platform final

First v4.0.1 cut where macOS and Windows ship the same self-contained app: full `foxora-engine` runtime bundled inside the installer, no external dependencies.

**Windows is now live.**
- `foxora_4.0.1_x64-setup.exe` — 80 MB NSIS, installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\foxora\`.
- Embeds Node.js 24.15.0 (matches the engine's `better-sqlite3` / `@libsql` NMV 137 ABI) so users without Node installed get a working engine out of the box.
- Embeds the WebView2 evergreen bootstrapper — installs work offline, on locked-down corporate machines, and on fresh Win10/11 images.
- Engine boots headless on first launch (no terminal window). Lives as a background child of `foxora-ai.exe`, listening on `127.0.0.1:4111`. Same model as macOS.
- Win10/11 hardening: COEP/COOP headers removed (WebView2 was rejecting them), Vite build target lowered to `chrome105`, boot-failure diagnostic overlay added (renders a recovery page with a WebView2 download link if React ever fails to mount).

**macOS — engine bundled.**
- Apple Silicon `.app` contains `Contents/Resources/foxora-engine/` (22,996 files, 312 MB). Self-contained — no dev-tree dependency.
- Notarized, stapled, Gatekeeper-accepted offline.
- `mastra → foxora-engine` rename for internal directory names and Rust-side lookup paths. Framework class still upstream `Mastra`.

**Updater key rotation.**
- Minisign pubkey baked into the app: `DE0AEE70D2308ABB` → `D492E3724E1D8E20`.
- Previous private key was lost; this build resets the channel with a fresh keypair (backed up).
- **Consequence: existing v4.0.1 installs must manually reinstall once** to receive future auto-updates. From v4.0.2 onward, auto-update is silent again.

**Native modules signed (macOS).**
- Six embedded native binaries (`.node` for `@libsql/darwin-arm64`, `better-sqlite3`, `fsevents`; `.bare` for `bare-fs`/`bare-os`/`bare-url`) get a Developer ID signature before notary submission. Foreign-arch prebuilds (iOS simulator, Android, Windows, Linux) pruned at stage time.

**One-command publish (macOS).** `bun run publish:update <version>` handles tar/sign/push/manifest in one shot.
